outcome: neonatal outcomes (low birth weight, stillbirth, neonatal death)
cohort: 50 pregnant women with spinal cord injuries attending the National Spinal Injury Centre at Buckinghamshire NHS Trust between 1991 and 2016
finding: Pregnancy outcomes were generally successful in women with spinal cord injuries, with vaginal delivery safely achieved in the majority of women, independent of the level of SCI.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was achieved in 77% of pregnancies, including 14% instrumental delivery rate and 23% Caesarean delivery rate.
